source.title: Understanding the Covariance Structure of Convolutional Filters
source.authors: Asher Trockman; Devin Willmott; J. Kolter

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a new convolutional-filter initialization with standard uniform initialization and reports effects on training speed and classification accuracy. It does not test the specific initialization methods or gradient and signal propagation mechanisms named in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for covariance transfer and its proposed initialization. Rows below focus on the proposed initialization versus uniform initialization, with the reported accuracy values and explicit convergence-speed findings. Cited prior-work results are not included.
record.test_reason: The study tests a structural covariance initialization for large depthwise filters in ConvMixer and ConvNeXt. Its results concern test accuracy and training budgets needed to reach test accuracy. These do not test V4's activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient preservation, or trainable depth in plain networks. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their inexpensive, learning-free covariance initialization typically improves accuracy and convergence for large depthwise filters, particularly in deeper models and shorter training. They also emphasize that initialized filters can sometimes remain frozen while matching or exceeding uniformly initialized models with trained filters. The text reports poor performance for 3×3 filters and reduced ImageNet accuracy for ConvNeXt-Atto.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a depth-dependent multivariate Gaussian covariance initialization for depthwise convolutional filters and compares it with uniform initialization; it does not reproduce the activation-matched or orthogonal initialization recipes in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported gains vary with model depth, architecture, patch and filter settings, and training duration; the initialization helped deeper ConvMixers but reduced accuracy for ConvNeXt-Atto. The paper says it performed poorly for 3×3 filters and that gains were often more prominent for shorter training.

fits_no_version.finding: Covariance initialization reduces the training budget needed for ConvMixer-256/16 to reach 90% CIFAR-10 test accuracy, approximately halving epochs relative to uniform initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured covariance initialization of large depthwise filters can reduce the training budget needed to reach a target test accuracy in ConvMixer.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet test-accuracy gains depend on architecture, depth, initialization parameters, and training duration; ConvNeXt-Atto loses accuracy at 50 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured covariance initialization often improves fixed-budget test accuracy in large-kernel depthwise networks, with architecture- and parameter-dependent exceptions.

record.problems: The paper reports classification accuracy rather than training classification error; it does not directly measure gradient or signal propagation. Some results are only in figures, and reported training experiments use three random seeds. Several initialization hyperparameters were selected through searches, with settings held fixed across differing architectures and filter sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were extracted from the CIFAR-10 accuracy figures and appendix tables, which report many separate model, kernel-size, epoch, initialization, and frozen/thawed combinations. The kept rows prioritize explicit convergence-speed text and the ImageNet comparisons in Table 1, including the reported negative case.

untested.parts: Training classification error, memorization of corrupted or random labels, and dependence on size, stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and additional student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain networks, identity-shortcut controls, and the stated initialization exceptions.

Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients in plain networks; learning speed and trainable depth under those conditions; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization; and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature evolution, edge of stability, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Larger test-accuracy gains at greater depth do not establish increased trainable depth or reduced training error. Additional CIFAR and appendix comparisons are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows under the supplied rule. Table 1 reports two initialization settings; the extracted rows switch between them without recording that condition.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization on training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, shortcut effects, and normalization removal.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation measurements, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, plain tanh networks, and training at 10,000 layers.
Learning-rate stability limits, loss increases and recovery, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free residual networks.

rows.subject: ConvMixer-256/16
rows.operation_detail: Compared proposed filter initialization with uniform initialization; reported epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.value: approximately 50% fewer epochs than uniform initialization
rows.note: The text also says the proposed initialization reached 90% in around 25% fewer epochs than direct learned-filter transfer.
rows.check: The reported 50% reduction concerns epochs needed to reach 90% test accuracy with covariance initialization, outside V4's specified initialization and network conditions. Figure 8 compares separate runs, each completing its learning-rate schedule; it is not a trajectory from one training run.

rows.subject: ConvMixer-256/16
rows.operation_detail: Compared proposed filter initialization with direct learned-filter transfer; reported epochs to reach 90% test accuracy.
rows.value: around 25% fewer epochs than direct learned-filter transfer
rows.check: The reported 25% reduction compares covariance initialization with transferred learned filters, outside V4. Each Figure 8 point represents a separate run completing its learning-rate schedule.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Thawed-filter ImageNet-1k models other than ConvNeXt-Atto, at 50 or 150 epochs
reader_labels.reason: Proposed initialization improves reported accuracy over uniform initialization in these conditions (R3–R9, R11–R13). The CIFAR-10 convergence comparison also reports fewer epochs to reach 90% accuracy (R1–R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The proposed initialization lowers reported accuracy relative to uniform initialization (R10).
